correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in z and y give the conditional laws. Exact polynomial generator identities imply \(\mathbb E[y]=\mathbb E[x^2]\). The negative-y region is invariant, so any stationary mass there would normalize to an invariant measure with negative mean y, contradicting the nonnegative mean-square identity. The y=0 subsystem has characteristic polynomial \(\lambda^2-\alpha\lambda+\beta\mu\); with positive parameters all eigenvalues have positive real part, hence its only bounded complete trajectory is the origin. This identifies the zero-plane mass and gives \(\mathbb E[x^2]=\mathbb E[y]=1-w\). The unit-cylinder equality case is incompatible with compact invariance because \(z\) would drift at nonzero constant speed. The packaged checker verifies all nonstandard algebraic identities.

value.rationale: The source emphasizes coexistence and strong initial-condition sensitivity, making global statements shared by every recurrent component mathematically useful. The result proves a parameter-independent selection rule excluding all compact stationary mass from \(y<0\), identifies a conditional unit-amplitude law on every positive-y slice, and converts the origin atomic mass into exact first/second moments. For every non-equilibrium recurrent component it forces genuine excursions on both sides of \(|x|=1\). These are structural recurrence constraints, not a recomputation of a Lyapunov exponent or an arbitrary finite slice.
